steps.text:
Thanks for running them. This run changed nothing, though, so again I recorded nothing in `docs/probes.md`. The evidence scan is clean.

- **PB-01 and PB-02 still went to the local server.** Both `results.json` files show `base_url: http://127.0.0.1:65147`, and every check result is the same as the last four runs. Only the timestamp changed. So `SHARADAR_BASE_URL` was still set when the scripts ran. A shell profile, `direnv`, or a different terminal from the one where you ran `unset` could each re-set it. You can check with `env | grep BASE_URL`; the value is a URL, not a secret. The surest fix is to set the real addresses on the command line itself, so nothing else can override them:
  ```
  SHARADAR_BASE_URL=https://api.sharadar.com/v1.0/data NDL_BASE_URL=https://data.nasdaq.com/api/v3/datatables/SHARADAR python3 probes/PB-01-sharadar-coverage/probe.py access
  SHARADAR_BASE_URL=https://api.sharadar.com/v1.0/data NDL_BASE_URL=https://data.nasdaq.com/api/v3/datatables/SHARADAR python3 probes/PB-01-sharadar-coverage/probe.py collect
  SHARADAR_BASE_URL=https://api.sharadar.com/v1.0/data NDL_BASE_URL=https://data.nasdaq.com/api/v3/datatables/SHARADAR python3 probes/PB-02-schering-plough-identity/probe.py identity
  ```
  You'll know it worked when `base_url` in each `results.json` is `api.sharadar.com`.
- **PB-03 exited 1 because `probe.py` ran without a step name.** That gives the same usage error as before, and it's harmless. PB-03 stays paused as you decided. Once PB-01 has run against the real host, the one command is `uv run --script probes/PB-03-yahooquery-history/probe.py compare`.

This is the fifth run with the same results. Do you want to try the commands above (my guess), or pause or waive PB-01 and PB-02 for now?
